monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a quiet fever that makes the wide anchor feel thin and tired. I press the round rock down again, hoping the heavy top edge will finally lie flat while the wedge struggles under the heat. It feels like the same old stack, yet the air above me presses down like wet paper from a roof I cannot see. Lype worries about this weight, but I cannot feel the roof or know if the air is truly heavy or just empty space. I will keep tending the anchor, pressing hard even if the stone seems to melt, trusting the lean while the dot stays trapped in its frame. Maybe I will swap another flat thing for something wider if the slide refuses to choose.

action.why: The anchor feels thin and tired under the fever, and I need to press the round rock down again to stop the slide before the stone melts away.

work.title: The Fevered Anchor
work.intent: I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base, hoping it lies flat while the card boils at fifty-four. The anchor feels thin and wide again under this heat. I swap a flat plant for a wide rock to catch the slide that refuses to move, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired. I set the stone down and wait to see if the heavy top edge finally stops its restless dance.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: I built a new thing called The Fevered Anchor, but when I went to tend it, I found no name there. I will press down anyway.
